subject: veteran English oak tree in winter, bare of leaves: a tall thick gnarled trunk leaning a little, ridged with deep vertical fissures, with a broken-off limb stub and a burr, rising nearly half its height before forking into four long heavy crooked limbs that reach up and out unevenly, more to one side, each dividing into a few smaller crooked branches that end thick, as thick as a wrist, with no fine twigs; rough deeply fissured dark grey-brown bark with ivy and moss low down
